title: TRICARE Prime Terms on Referrals, Routine Eye Exams and Claim Filing
content:
**TRICARE Prime** tiers state whether non-emergency specialty care and network urgent care need a referral from the primary care manager (PCM), how often a routine eye exam is covered without a referral, and how long after the date of service a claim may be filed.

| Tier | Non-emergency specialty care needs a PCM referral | Network urgent care needs a referral | Months between covered routine eye exams without a referral | Claim filing deadline (calendar days after the date of service) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TRICARE Prime Active Duty Service Member | yes | no | 12 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Remote Active Duty Service Member | yes | no | 12 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Active Duty Family Member | yes | no | 12 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Remote Active Duty Family Member | yes | no | 12 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Transitional Survivor | yes | no | 12 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Retiree Group A | yes | no | 24 | 365 |
| TRICARE Prime Retiree Group B | yes | no | 24 | 365 |

## Reading the table

- In every tier, non-emergency specialty care needs a PCM referral, while a network urgent care visit does not.
- The routine eye exam interval is 12 months for the five active duty, active duty family member and transitional survivor tiers and 24 months for the two retiree tiers.
- A claim is filed in time when it is filed within 365 calendar days after the date of service, in every tier.
